source.title: Stronger generalization bounds for deep nets via a compression approach
source.authors: Sanjeev Arora; Rong Ge; Behnam Neyshabur; Yi Zhang

record.file_problem: none; full paper text and appendices are present
record.tranche_reason: Empirically measures network properties and their association with generalization on normally and randomly labeled data; it does not reproduce the claim versions’ interventions or measures.
record.gate_note: Reports CIFAR-10 accuracy for VGG-19 and AlexNet on natural labels and AlexNet on shuffled labels, plus network-property measurements during training and comparisons between the natural-label and shuffled-label AlexNets. Figure 1’s layer-wise injected-noise values and Figure 2’s property distributions are presented as plots without precise numerical results in the text; no rows are extracted from them. The paper’s comparisons to other bounds are not outcomes of the claim’s behaviors.
record.test_reason: Section 6 directly repeats the natural-label versus shuffled-label training and held-out accuracy comparison underlying V1. AlexNet fits both training sets perfectly but generalizes only with natural labels. The recipe includes explicit regularization.
record.authors_conclusion: The record's paraphrase is broadly accurate. The authors derive compression-based generalization bounds using empirically verified noise-stability properties, including for convolutional networks. Their measure captures only part of the observed generalization trend. The theoretical guarantees generally concern the compressed network, and empirical bound comparisons omit depth, logarithmic, and other nuisance factors.
record.recipe_differences: The study uses SGD and explicit weight decay and dropout to train CIFAR-10 networks, then measures accuracy and proposed noise-stability properties. It does not replicate the version’s listed Zhang et al. random-label experiment or its specified unregularized recipes.
record.method_sensitivity: The paper reports property differences for natural versus randomly shuffled labels and improvement in the proposed bound and test error across training epochs. Exact plotted values are not stated.

fits_no_version.finding: The natural-label AlexNet has larger layer cushion and smaller activation contraction than its shuffled-label counterpart.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: Noise-stability properties distinguish these natural-label and shuffled-label AlexNets in directions consistent with the proposed compression bound.

fits_no_version.finding: VGG-19 test error and the proposed bound improve after training error becomes nearly zero; the bound captures only part of the improvement and is rescaled in the plot.
fits_no_version.proposed_claim: The proposed compression measure tracks part of the generalization improvement during training.

record.problems: Only one dataset is used for the reported accuracy results. The natural-label versus shuffled-label comparison uses AlexNet; no paired VGG-19 shuffled-label result is reported. No uncertainty estimates are stated. Property and bound trends are largely presented in figures, with few precise numerical values in text.
record.rows_left_out: Figure 1 reports injected-noise attenuation by layer for VGG-19, and Figures 2, 4, and Appendix D show property distributions or bound comparisons primarily as plots. Their precise values are not stated in the text, so no separate rows are extracted from those figures.

untested.parts: Unregularized training recipes; paired random-label VGG-19 results; Inception models, MLPs, and ImageNet.
Convolutional versus fully connected accuracy and the contribution of local connectivity.
Adaptive versus nonadaptive optimizers and tuning-dependent differences.
Batch-size interventions and recipe adaptations under fixed epoch budgets.
Dropout interventions; using dropout alone does not test its effect.
Magnitude-aware weight sharpness, its association with generalization gaps, and its ranking against other measures.
Removal of memorized examples versus random removal and subsequent retraining.

record.verdict_notes: Remove the reader's V1 limits_scope verdict based on R4–R5: a different property measure does not establish a failure or qualification of V1. Explicit regularization is a tested recipe difference, not evidence against the coexistence claim.

versions.untested_parts: Tests VGG-19 and AlexNet on CIFAR-10 with natural labels and AlexNet with randomly shuffled labels. Does not test the listed Inception models, MLPs, or other training recipes.

conditions.value: initial 0.05, decayed by factor 2 every 30 epochs

rows.subject: AlexNet trained on normal CIFAR-10
rows.operation_detail: Compared layer-cushion and activation-contraction distributions between the AlexNet trained on normal data and the AlexNet trained on corrupted data.

conditions.value: CIFAR-10, normal versus randomly shuffled labels

rows.measure: Layer cushion and activation contraction, associated by the authors with generalization
rows.baseline: AlexNet trained on corrupted dataset; exact values not stated
rows.value: The normal-data net has larger layer cushion and smaller activation contraction.
rows.note: Comparison is reported qualitatively; the plotted distributions do not provide textually stated precise values.
rows.check: Layer cushion and activation contraction do not measure V1's memorization and held-out accuracy outcomes. They also do not measure V7's magnitude-scaled weight sharpness.

rows.baseline: AlexNet trained on normal dataset; exact values not stated
rows.value: The corrupted-data net has smaller layer cushion and larger activation contraction.
rows.note: Comparison is reported qualitatively; the plotted distributions do not provide textually stated precise values.

rows.subject: VGG-19
rows.operation_detail: Tracked the proposed generalization bound and empirical error during training.
rows.measure: Training error, test error, and proposed generalization bound
rows.baseline: After 120 epochs, training error is almost zero; exact values not stated.
rows.value: Test error continues to improve in later epochs; the proposed bound also improves, though not to the same level.
rows.note: This reports a training-time trend in error and the authors’ bound; it does not provide the claim version’s defined intervention or a numerical training-test gap.
rows.check: Correctly unlinked. Training duration and the proposed compression bound are different from V2's width intervention and V7's sharpness measure. Figure 4 rescales the bound for visual comparison.
